Description: Balanced load: A medium-density matrix with very low variance in row lengths, representing a structurally uniform and predictable workload.
High density: A relatively compact but dense matrix with a large number of non-zeros per row, generating heavy computational volume per row.
Mild irregularity: Introduces early structural irregularities, providing a stepping stone between balanced and skewed datasets.
Uniform structure: Features near-zero variance. Every row contains almost exactly the same amount of elements, completely eliMiating load imbalances.
Standard baseline: A model matrix with medium-low density, serving as reliable middle-ground test case for general validation.
Heavy memory footprint: A dense matrix with a massive total number of non-zeros relative to its dimensions, acting as a stress-test for memory bandwidth.
Extreme sparsity: A very large graph with extremely few elements per row, representing a scenario dominated by structural navigation rather than computation.
Severe irregularity: A social network graph with extreme variance in row lengths, presenting a highly challenging load-balancing scenario.
Big Data scale: The largest dataset in the suite, used to evaluate structural handling and memory allocation limits on massive, multi-million-row topologies.
Real-world graph: Reflects the typical topology of web-routing and information retrieval graphs, offering an intermediate test for irregular sparsity patterns.
